verdict.reasoning: Patient describes symptoms for "a few days" and doctor summarizes as "the last four days"; rash is "mostly like my chest, my...hands, my arms...inside the elbows" and patient confirms "No" involvement of the face.
Patient reports "my skin is a bit cracked in some parts" and denies "any other pus or blood coming out of your skin?" with response "No," indicating cracked skin without bleeding or discharge.

Patient states prior eczema and wonders if this is eczema again: "So I had eczema before, so maybe it's this"; doctor says "I do wonder whether this is a flare up of your eczema," describing it as an exacerbation.
Patient: "earlier I was like prescribed for my eczema and they gave me like some cream..." and when asked if it helped: "at that time? Yes," indicating past steroid/eczema creams were effective.
Patient: "I bought like a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night, but it apparently didn't help because it's still itching a lot today."

Patient says "I can't even sleep at night" and at work "I can't actually think about what I have to say. I'm always like, disturbed by this disease," showing severe itch interfering with sleep and concentration.

When asked about fever: "have you noticed any temperature or fevers?" Patient: "No. Just the itching"; about chest/cough/breathing: "No cough? No. Breathing difficulties?" Patient: "No"; about urine: "You're passing urine Okay?" Patient: "I think so."
Patient repeatedly notes past eczema: "earlier I was like prescribed for my eczema" and "So I had eczema before."
When asked about other medical problems, patient says: "No, I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore?"
Doctor: "And do you take any regular medications at the moment?" Patient: "No."
Doctor: "Do you have any allergies at all?" Patient: "Oh, allergies. No."
Patient: "So I live with a few flatmates...I'm living with a few people to save money."
Patient: "So you know, I'm 31."
Patient: "I have a full time job" and "I work at a pharmaceutical company...I'm a...like a kind of project manager."
Patient: "once in a while...a few beers per week...Nothing crazy. I used to drink a lot more when I was younger."
Doctor: "do you smoke at all?" Patient: "No."

Doctor says, "Normally at this stage, I like to examine you... But from what you've told me... And having looked at your skin, the rash does appear quite familiar," indicating a skin examination (likely via video) was performed, not that it could not be performed.
Doctor summarizes: "you mentioned you've got some dry skin and some cracked skin as well," consistent with same rash distribution previously described (chest, hands, inside elbows).

Doctor: "I do wonder whether this is a flare up of your eczema. The reason being that you said it's quite itchy. It's mainly affecting your chest and your back. And having looked at your skin, the rash does appear quite familiar," reflecting a likely eczema flare with pruritic, cracked skin on trunk/arms/hands.
Doctor: "I wonder whether giving you stronger prescription of a steroid may be beneficial, which I'm happy to prescribe to you today."
Doctor: "as well as I'm going to give you something, some emollients which helps to moisturize the skin to use in the bath and shower."

After patient says OTC antihistamines didn't help, doctor: "I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well. Something like fexofenadine, which I can give to you today. It's definitely worth trying it."
Doctor: "It's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms. Anything you wear or anything you use in terms of shower gels or soap."

Doctor: "it's definitely worth using that for the first seven to 10 days before we make a decision on whether it's working or not" and later "do come back and see me next week if things don't get better," implying follow-up in about 7–10 days.
